On 14 January 2019, a [Boeing 707](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_707) operated by [Saha Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saha_Airlines) on a [cargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cargo) flight crashed at [Fath Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fath_Air_Base), near [Karaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaj), [Alborz province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alborz_province) in Iran.[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1)[[2]](#cite_note-caffeinamagazine-2) The aircraft was the last civil Boeing 707 in operation.

The aircraft involved was a [Boeing 707](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_707)-3J9C, c/n 21128, [registration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_registration) EP-CPP.[[3]](#cite_note-AH4c2d9613-3) The aircraft was owned by the [Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Republic_of_Iran_Air_Force) and had been leased to Saha Airlines.[[4]](#cite_note-ASN-4) The aircraft was 42 years old at the time.[[5]](#cite_note-Nine140119-5) The aircraft had first flown on 19 November 1976, and was delivered that month to the [Imperial Iranian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Iranian_Air_Force) as 5–8312. It had been transferred to Saha Airlines on 27 February 2000, and was re-registered EP-SHK. It was substantially damaged by an [uncontained engine failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncontained_engine_failure) on 3 August 2009, whilst on a flight from [Ahvaz International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahvaz_International_Airport) to [Mehrabad International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehrabad_International_Airport), [Tehran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran). An emergency landing was made at Ahvaz; the aircraft was subsequently repaired. It was returned to the IRIAF in December 2015 and returned to Saha Airlines in May 2016, registered EP-CPP.[[6]](#cite_note-ASN030809-6)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2019_Saha_Airlines_Boeing_707_crash_46.jpgTail wreckage of EP-CPP

The aircraft was on an international cargo flight carrying meat from [Manas International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manas_International_Airport) in [Bishkek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishkek), [Kyrgyzstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyzstan), to [Payam International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payam_International_Airport)[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1) in [Karaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaj), Iran, but the flight crew actually landed at Fath Air Base. The crew probably mistook Fath Air Base's runway for the much longer Payam International Airport runway,[[7]](#cite_note-AH4c2d96132-7)[[8]](#cite_note-Nine1401192-8) as the two runways are just a few kilometres apart and on a similar alignment. A 707 generally requires a runway length more than 2,500 m (8,200 ft),[[2]](#cite_note-caffeinamagazine-2) but the runway at Fath Air Base is only 1,300 metres (4,300 ft).[[9]](#cite_note-9) Poor weather conditions were also reported.[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10)

The aircraft overran the runway, crashed through a wall, and came to rest after colliding with a house in the neighbourhood of Farrokhabad, Fardis County, [Alborz province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alborz_province). The accident was captured on Security footage and shows the plane as it crashes and bursts into flames. The houses involved were empty at the time of the crash,[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10)[[11]](#cite_note-IRNA83170453-11) and no one on the ground was injured.[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10) Fifteen of the sixteen crew on board were killed; one crew member survived, but was seriously injured. There were no passengers.[[12]](#cite_note-12) Following the crash, a fire developed. Early reports gave the number of people on board as either 16 or 17, all but one of whom died.[[13]](#cite_note-TT431837-13) The sole survivor was Farshad Mahdavinejad, the aircraft's flight engineer, who was taken to Shariati Hospital in a critical condition.[[5]](#cite_note-Nine140119-5)

In a possibly related incident from 16 November 2018, a Taban Airlines MD-88 carrying 155 people twice attempted to land on this runway, mistaking it for the longer 3,659 metres (12,005 ft) Payam runway, which is nearly inline. On the first approach the plane reached an altitude of 1 metre (3.3 ft) before aborting the attempt, but eventually continued on for a safe landing at Payam after an aborted second attempt there.[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1)

An investigation was opened into the accident.[[5]](#cite_note-Nine140119-5) The [cockpit voice recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockpit_voice_recorder) was recovered from the wreckage on 14 January.[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10) The [flight data recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_data_recorder) and the [control display unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_management_system) were also recovered.[[3]](#cite_note-AH4c2d9613-3)

On 28 February, AIRAC Cycle 02/2019 was released with all approach charts for Payam Airport having been modified to show Fath Airport along with the following note: "Do not mistake Fath and Naja Airports for Payam Airport which have similar runway alignments."[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1)

It was returned to the IRIAF in December 2015 and returned to Saha Airlines in May 2016, registered EP-CPP.[[6]](#cite_note-ASN030809-6)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2019_Saha_Airlines_Boeing_707_crash_46.jpgTail wreckage of EP-CPP

The aircraft was on an international cargo flight carrying meat from [Manas International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manas_International_Airport) in [Bishkek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishkek), [Kyrgyzstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyzstan), to [Payam International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payam_International_Airport)[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1) in [Karaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karaj), Iran, but the flight crew actually landed at Fath Air Base. The crew probably mistook Fath Air Base's runway for the much longer Payam International Airport runway,[[7]](#cite_note-AH4c2d96132-7)[[8]](#cite_note-Nine1401192-8) as the two runways are just a few kilometres apart and on a similar alignment. A 707 generally requires a runway length more than 2,500 m (8,200 ft),[[2]](#cite_note-caffeinamagazine-2) but the runway at Fath Air Base is only 1,300 metres (4,300 ft).[[9]](#cite_note-9) Poor weather conditions were also reported.[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10)

The aircraft overran the runway, crashed through a wall, and came to rest after colliding with a house in the neighbourhood of Farrokhabad, Fardis County, [Alborz province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alborz_province). The accident was captured on Security footage and shows the plane as it crashes and bursts into flames. The houses involved were empty at the time of the crash,[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10)[[11]](#cite_note-IRNA83170453-11) and no one on the ground was injured.[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10) Fifteen of the sixteen crew on board were killed; one crew member survived, but was seriously injured. There were no passengers.[[12]](#cite_note-12) Following the crash, a fire developed. Early reports gave the number of people on board as either 16 or 17, all but one of whom died.[[13]](#cite_note-TT431837-13) The sole survivor was Farshad Mahdavinejad, the aircraft's flight engineer, who was taken to Shariati Hospital in a critical condition.[[5]](#cite_note-Nine140119-5)

In a possibly related incident from 16 November 2018, a Taban Airlines MD-88 carrying 155 people twice attempted to land on this runway, mistaking it for the longer 3,659 metres (12,005 ft) Payam runway, which is nearly inline. On the first approach the plane reached an altitude of 1 metre (3.3 ft) before aborting the attempt, but eventually continued on for a safe landing at Payam after an aborted second attempt there.[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1)

An investigation was opened into the accident.[[5]](#cite_note-Nine140119-5) The [cockpit voice recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockpit_voice_recorder) was recovered from the wreckage on 14 January.[[10]](#cite_note-BBC46861324-10) The [flight data recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_data_recorder) and the [control display unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_management_system) were also recovered.[[3]](#cite_note-AH4c2d9613-3)

On 28 February, AIRAC Cycle 02/2019 was released with all approach charts for Payam Airport having been modified to show Fath Airport along with the following note: "Do not mistake Fath and Naja Airports for Payam Airport which have similar runway alignments."[[1]](#cite_note-rainews-1)

content.text: The sole survivor was **Farshad Mahdavinejad**, the flight engineer.

Written to `answer.txt`: **Farshad Mahdavinejad** — the flight engineer of Saha Airlines Flight 5054 (Boeing 707-3J9C, EP-CPP), which overran the runway at Fath Air Base on 14 January 2019 after mistaking it for Payam Airport. 15 of the 16 crew died; he was the sole survivor.
